findings.title: The launch requirement's refusal row names only the trail reader, not the save's two new refusals
findings.recommendation: Walk 2 gave orbit external save two more refusals — a return the report renderer rejects, and an aliased change directory or trail — and recorded both in orbit-external-runner's save table. The launch requirement in orbit-review-external closes its domain over failure rows, and its refusal row still reads 'no unfenced heading, names another change, or is rejected by the trail reader'. The body is right (Step 9d treats ANY save refusal as a failed run), so this is the row's wording only: widen it to 'or is refused by orbit external save for any other cause (per orbit-external-runner's save table)'.

findings.title: After a failed handoff push, the fallback's handoff-blocked text tells the user to commit a prompt that is already committed
findings.recommendation: On the launch route the prompt and T0 are committed in Step 9a before the push; when that push fails and the run then fails, the fallback prints Step 8's handoff-blocked output, which leads 'Commit the pending work (including the prompt file above) and push'. Only the push is pending. Name the launch-route variant in the failed-run paragraph: 'Handoff blocked: the handoff commit <short-sha> is not pushed. Push, then hand off: …'.

commentary: Graded both walk logs against the generated reference, the two delta specs and the engine code. Every resolved entry is present at each site it claims: the -F commit form appears in the body, the launched-return requirement and the harness (which now runs the message through a real shell with a $(...) and backtick preamble that must not execute); the failed-run fallback carries the session note and the Repo correction, with the apply-after-launch case split out; the subshell and the repository-root anchor are both stated; the recovery line keeps --launch and the cleanup. The new renderer import closes no load-order problem: config list/set/unset, external runner and status all ran under a scratch config home, and unset of the preset now leaves no empty record. The residual check from the commit that added the external return lists eleven files, all inside the walks' edit records. Both remaining notes sit beside the walks' edits rather than in them: a domain row that names one of the save's three refusal kinds, and a pre-existing fallback string that predates the walk.
